description: workspace_invitations has no unique constraint on (workspace_id, email), so two concurrent invite requests for the same person race each other at the database level and both succeed, creating duplicate pending invitations instead of one being rejected.

required_findings.justification: There is no `unique (workspace_id, email)` constraint (or equivalent partial unique index scoped to pending status) anywhere in this table definition. An application-level 'check for an existing invite, then insert' pattern cannot close this race by itself — two concurrent requests can both pass the check before either insert commits — so only a database-level constraint actually prevents duplicate pending invitations for the same email in the same workspace.

explanation: A genuine database-layer concurrency defect: the fix is a database constraint, not application code, and the flaw is only visible by noticing what's ABSENT from the table definition (no unique constraint) rather than any single wrong line — the ground truth spans the whole create table statement for that reason.
